posts.name: WalkingTarget
posts.cooked: Assuming I’m the only one, no more sleep. So much more stuff I could get done/personal time.

posts.name: Rabit
posts.cooked: I have far too many interesting and useful dreams to avoid sleeping, personally (although I get the allure). It would be wonderful to no longer need to eat, though, saving me a lot of time, energy, and expense.

posts.name: WalkingTarget
posts.cooked:
Eating was my choice if it was “if nobody has to do it again” as it frees up all kinds of resources worldwide. Nobody needing to sleep I fear would just cause everybody to have an expectation to work twice as much.

I also almost never remember my dreams, so not dreaming isn’t a big loss for me.

Yeah, I knew someone would choose sleep.

My Answer to Yesterday’s Question: I’d don’t really want to forgo the pleasant aspects of eating, drinking, and sleeping (yes, I know that I still could partake in them, but I’d have less motivation to do so), so I’ll say breathing. No drowning!

fjur’s Questions of the Day #58: Would you rather be able to speak/read/write et cetera all languages, or instantaneously travel to all countries on Earth?

posts.name: WalkingTarget
posts.cooked: Understanding all languages is something I’ve voiced a desire for often. I’d much rather be able to understand everything and then have to travel normally than be able to travel instantly and be unable to communicate effectively once there. Plus, I can get a fair amount of use out of the language ability even without traveling extensively. Teleportation is a tempting alternate choice, though, but it depends on the restrictions that your prompt implies. Like, being able to teleport around arbitrarily (say, so that I could attend Gen Con while still sleeping in my own bed every night) would be nice, but the wording implies to me that the power gets me to any country, but then I’m stuck navigating within it on my own.

WalkingTarget:

Though it’s probably important to note whether we’re dealing with Hunted Naturalist or default Naturalist in his woodchuck-form as a Rhino-Croc Woodchuck would chuck far more would than a woodchuck should chuck with a woodchuck was The Naturalist in his default woodchuck-form.

fjur’s Questions of the Day #60: Do you prefer warm or cold beverages?

posts.name: Rabit
posts.cooked:
Uh…

All of the above?
I love warm drinks – going to get myself some hot chocolate in a couple of minutes, in fact. However, I also appreciate a lot of cold drinks, especially alcoholic (although I really shouldn’t drink them ). And I almost always have a room-temperature water bottle with me, as I drink a lot of water!

I actually tried to post an answer to yesterday’s question, but the forum would not allow me to post “ALL THE WOOD!!! ”

ALL THE WOOD!!!

Edit: Huh, it allowed me to.

I actually prefer beverages at room temperature. If a soda or something tastes better cold, I tend to assume that it just tastes bad, and my taste buds are numbed so I can’t tell. Hot beverages are a rarity, because I don’t want to be bothered with the effort of preparing them; I probably drink cold things more often, because I buy a 20oz bottle out of a refrigerator case, but I would usually like them just as much if I waited four hours to drink them.

My Answer to Yesterday’s Question: I, too, enjoy both of them.

posts.cooked: I’d go with being able to shift into animal forms. The first thing that comes to mind for turning into humans is evil deeds that can be committed. But animals, that’d be bundles of fun.

My Answer to Yesterday’s Question: Argh, I don’t have an answer prepared for this one. I agree with @The_Justifier that human-shifting can have many opportunities to be useful nowadays, but so does animal-shifting, but in different ways! And I agree with @Ronway that human-shifting has great criminal potential, but so does animal-shifting, albeit to a lesser extent. Argh! Indecision! Well, I guess that since “with Great Power comes Great Responsibility” and all that, if I had either of those powers, I’d need to become a superhero. So, in that case, humans, because I don’t want to tread on The Naturalist’s turf.
